tasks.short: Read new offenders' files, collect medical, separation and release information, decide which issues need special attention, record measures for officers, and discuss complex cases.

steps.what: Correctional supervisor reviews offender information in files, court documents and transfer notes
Correctional supervisor collects medical, separation and release-date information from several systems and e-mails
Correctional supervisor identifies issues that require special attention and decides measures
Correctional supervisor writes the measures in the unit log for officers
Correctional supervisor discusses complex cases with the medical and psychological services

tasks.design: The records app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows fixed-rule flags on each offender's page for medical alerts, separation orders, release dates and court dates, taken from the source systems, so the supervisor reads the flagged items first and does not collect them from several systems and e-mails. Measures are recorded on the same page and shown to officers on the unit screen instead of a paper log. No risk score is computed; deciding special attention stays with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information sat in several systems and e-mails and measures were written in a paper log.
tasks.enabler_now: Records apps can show rule-based flags from linked systems.
tasks.still_hard: Information that arrives late by phone is not flagged.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing that a new arrival is at risk despite a clean file.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor judges flagged issues instead of collecting them.

reach.learn: Whether measures reach them in time.

evidence.claim: Records apps can show rule-based flags such as medical alerts, separation orders and release dates.
Crime-risk prediction based solely on profiling is banned; no risk score is used.
Decisions about people may not rest solely on automated processing.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new arrival to cases discussed; sentence planning is outside.
Input contract: source systems linked; fallback is reading files and e-mails.

The supervisor reads every flagged item and the full file for new arrivals, so s1 keeps 90; s2 keeps 30 because flags come from the source systems instead of e-mails; s4 keeps 90 because the offender's page replaces copying details into the paper log and the supervisor still writes each measure, an ordinary save on the same page.

incremental.description: Correctional supervisor reports wrong or missing flags.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only some source systems are linked, so much is still collected by e-mail and s2 keeps 60 (11.5); high: source systems linked (17.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect incidents and rule changes, discuss with officers, write the procedure, check it, publish it, and explain it at briefings.

steps.what: Correctional supervisor collects incidents, findings and rule changes that call for a procedure
Correctional supervisor discusses the procedure with officers and security staff
Correctional supervisor develops the work or security procedure text

loop.input: The supervisor's outline of the agreed steps, the current procedure and the library of rule texts.
loop.output: A draft procedure in the house format.
loop.check: Every rule reference must match an article in the rule text library or it is dropped; steps are taken only from the outline; the supervisor reads each section against the outline and the cited article for meaning and edits every section.
loop.stop: One draft per procedure; if rejected, the supervisor writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template gives the format, not the wording of the steps.

steps.what: Correctional supervisor checks the final procedure as its owner: each step against the agreed outline and the cited articles, and the officers it applies to
Correctional supervisor publishes the checked procedure: by e-mail to officers today, as a new version in the document system after the change
Correctional supervisor explains the procedure at shift briefings

tasks.design: The records app lists incidents and inspection findings by type, and rule changes arrive as notices, so inputs are not collected from the mailbox. A bounded step drafts the procedure from the supervisor's outline and the rule text library; references not found in the library are dropped and the supervisor edits every section. The supervisor checks the procedure as owner and publishes it once as a new version in the document system ({DOCS}), which notifies officers. Discussing and explaining the procedure stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures were written from scratch and sent as attachments.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft text whose references can be checked against a rule library.
tasks.still_hard: Procedures must fit the building and staffing of each unit.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a procedure officers will actually follow.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor edits procedures instead of writing them from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether they have the current version.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft procedures whose rule references can be checked against a library of rule texts.
Public tasks are not a works council matter, but their effects on staff work are.

assumptions: Boundary: from the procedure need to officers informed; policy set by the ministry is outside.
Input contract: rule text library kept current; fallback is writing from scratch.
The supervisor checks every procedure before publishing; s5 keeps 20 for the publishing.
research_questions: How much of each drafted procedure is kept?

incremental.description: Correctional supervisor reports outdated rule texts.

approvals.approved_version: The procedure text exactly as checked by the supervisor in s4, published once as a new version in the document system for the officers it applies to; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one new procedure for a unique unit, so the draft helps little and s1 keeps 80, s3 keeps 85 (11.0); high: routine updates after rule changes (23.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Listen to the complaint, decide to resolve or escalate, write the complaint note, check it, send it to the superior, chase the answer, and tell the complainant.

steps.what: Correctional supervisor listens to officers' or inmates' complaints
Correctional supervisor decides whether to resolve the complaint or escalate it
Correctional supervisor writes the complaint note for superiors
Correctional supervisor checks the final complaint note: facts and people against what was heard, and the superior it goes to
Correctional supervisor conveys the checked complaint to superiors: by e-mail today, by one release to the superior's queue after the change
Correctional supervisor phones the superior about the answer
Correctional supervisor tells the complainant the answer

tasks.design: Complaints are recorded on a form in the records app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with the type, the people involved and the facts, instead of a free-text note. The supervisor checks the note and releases it once to the superior's queue in a complaint register ({WORKFLOW}) with a due date, and its status shows there, so the supervisor phones only when an answer is late. Listening, deciding and telling the complainant stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complaints were written as notes, e-mailed and chased by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Complaint registers route cases and show status and due dates.
tasks.still_hard: Formal inmate complaints follow their own legal procedure.
tasks.human_edge: Calming an angry inmate while taking the complaint seriously.

evidence.claim: Complaint registers can route cases with due dates and show their status.
Inmates have a legal right to file formal complaints under national rules; those follow their own procedure.

assumptions: Boundary: from the complaint raised to the complainant told; formal complaint procedures are outside.
Input contract: superiors work from the register; fallback is e-mail.
The supervisor checks every note before it is sent. s3 keeps 80 because type and people are picked and the facts are still written; s5 keeps 20 for the release; s6 keeps 40 for late answers.

incremental.description: Correctional supervisor keeps complaint types current.

approvals.approved_version: The complaint note with type, people involved and facts exactly as checked by the supervisor in s4, sent once to the named superior's queue in the complaint register; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few complaints are escalated and superiors still answer by phone, so s3 keeps 95 and s6 keeps 80 (5.5); high: many complaints escalated each week (10.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count out tools and inmates at the workshop, supervise inmates at work, handle incidents, and record hours worked for pay.

steps.what: Correctional supervisor counts out tools and checks inmates in at the workshop: by hand today, by scanning tool tags against the inmate's pass at check-in and check-out after the change
Correctional supervisor supervises offenders performing maintenance, laundry, kitchen or workshop tasks
Correctional supervisor handles incidents and conflicts at work
Correctional supervisor records hours worked per inmate for pay: on a paper list today; after the change corrects the hours the check-in and check-out recorded
Correctional supervisor checks the period's hours per inmate against the work periods and known absences
Correctional supervisor releases the checked hours to the inmate wage administration

tasks.design: Tools carry tags and are issued by scanning against the inmate's pass in the workshop register ({OPS_SYSTEM}), which shows any tool not returned, so tools are not counted out and in by hand. The same check-in and check-out record each inmate's actual hours; the supervisor checks them and releases them once to the inmate wage administration instead of a paper list. Supervising work and handling incidents stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tools were counted by hand and hours kept on paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Tag scanning registers tool issue and inmate hours.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing tension in a work group before it turns into a fight.

evidence.claim: Tag scanning can register tool issue and return per person and show missing tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work period to hours recorded; work allocation is outside.
Input contract: tools tagged and passes issued; fallback is counting by hand.
Supervising does not change. s1 keeps 60 for scanning tools and passes; s4 keeps 30 for correcting hours; the hours check and release keep their full time.

approvals.approved_version: The period's hours per inmate exactly as checked by the supervisor in s4b, released once to the inmate wage administration for that period; any correction needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a kitchen with few tools where tags often fail, so s1 keeps 85 (8.1); high: a workshop with many tools and inmates (13.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The correctional supervisor keeps judging offender issues, agreeing procedures, hearing complaints and supervising work; collecting information, writing procedures from scratch, chasing answers and counting tools shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor with more time on the units.
